subproblem.title: Upper semicontinuity of closed-ball mass: {y : s ≤ μ(B̄_ρ(y))} is closed for a finite measure (parent step 4(i))
subproblem.statement: Let P ∈ ℕ, μ a finite measure on ℝ^P (Borel σ-algebra), ρ ∈ ℝ and s ∈ [0, ∞]. Then the set {y ∈ ℝ^P : s ≤ μ(B̄_ρ(y))} is closed, where B̄_ρ(y) = {z : |z − y| ≤ ρ} is the closed ball.
subproblem.lean_statement: ∀ (P : ℕ) (μ : Measure (Euclid P)) [IsFiniteMeasure μ] (ρ : ℝ) (s : ℝ≥0∞), IsClosed {y : Euclid P | s ≤ μ (closedBall y ρ)}
subproblem.natural_proof:
Source: parent proof, step 4(i). Closedness of the sets A_k there replaces the measurability of Simon's functions f_k (Simon Ch. 3, proof of 1.6 “⇐”, (7)–(8)).

1. Reduction. ℝ^P is a metric space, hence a sequential space, so it suffices to show that the set is sequentially closed. Let (y_i)_{i∈ℕ} satisfy s ≤ μ(B̄_ρ(y_i)) for every i and y_i → y; we prove s ≤ μ(B̄_ρ(y)).
2. Complements. Put U := ℝ^P ∖ B̄_ρ(y) and U_i := ℝ^P ∖ B̄_ρ(y_i). Closed balls are closed, so U and the U_i are open, hence Borel.
3. Pointwise liminf bound. For every z ∈ ℝ^P, 1_U(z) ≤ liminf_i 1_{U_i}(z). If z ∉ U, the left side is 0. If z ∈ U, then |z − y| > ρ. Since |z − y_i| → |z − y| (continuity of the distance), |z − y_i| > ρ for all sufficiently large i, i.e. z ∈ U_i eventually. So 1_{U_i}(z) = 1 for all large i, and the liminf equals 1.
4. Fatou. The functions 1_{U_i} are measurable and nonnegative. By Fatou's lemma (Mathlib `lintegral_liminf_le`) and step 3, μ(U) = ∫ 1_U dμ ≤ ∫ liminf_i 1_{U_i} dμ ≤ liminf_i ∫ 1_{U_i} dμ = liminf_i μ(U_i).
5. Bounding μ(U_i). Since μ is finite and B̄_ρ(y_i) is measurable, μ(U_i) = μ(ℝ^P) − μ(B̄_ρ(y_i)) ≤ μ(ℝ^P) − s. Here truncated subtraction on [0, ∞] is antitone in the subtracted argument, and s ≤ μ(B̄_ρ(y_i)). Every term is bounded by μ(ℝ^P) − s, so liminf_i μ(U_i) ≤ μ(ℝ^P) − s, and by step 4, μ(U) ≤ μ(ℝ^P) − s.
6. Conclusion. s ≤ μ(B̄_ρ(y_0)) ≤ μ(ℝ^P) < ∞. As μ is finite and B̄_ρ(y) is measurable, μ(B̄_ρ(y)) = μ(ℝ^P) − μ(U) ≥ μ(ℝ^P) − (μ(ℝ^P) − s) = s. The last equality uses s ≤ μ(ℝ^P) < ∞. Hence y belongs to the set, which is therefore closed. ∎
proof_key_steps: Sequential closedness suffices in the metric space ℝ^P: take y_i → y with s ≤ μ(B̄_ρ(y_i)).
The open complements satisfy 1_U ≤ liminf 1_{U_i} pointwise, where U = ℝ^P ∖ B̄_ρ(y) and U_i = ℝ^P ∖ B̄_ρ(y_i).
Fatou: μ(U) ≤ liminf μ(U_i) ≤ μ(ℝ^P) − s.
Finite measure: μ(B̄_ρ(y)) = μ(ℝ^P) − μ(U) ≥ s, using s ≤ μ(ℝ^P).

audit.reason: The complete sequential-closedness proof matches the exact type. Eventual membership in open complements gives the Fatou inequality; finite total mass validates both complement subtraction and cancellation. The sequence hypothesis forces s to be finite, covering s = ∞ without an omitted case. No positivity assumption on ρ is needed.

subproblem.title: Lower semicontinuity of cone mass along a continuous plane field: {x ∈ F : μ(X(x) ∩ B_ρ(x)) ≤ s} is closed (parent step 4(ii))
subproblem.statement: Let P ∈ ℕ, μ any measure on ℝ^P (Borel σ-algebra), and F ⊆ ℝ^P a closed set. Let Q : ℝ^P → linear subspaces of ℝ^P be such that x ↦ p_{Q(x)} (orthogonal projection onto Q(x), an element of L(ℝ^P) with the operator norm) is continuous on F. Let ρ ∈ ℝ and s ∈ [0, ∞]. For x ∈ ℝ^P put X(x) := {z : 2|p_{Q(x)}(z − x)| < |z − x|} and B_ρ(x) := {z : |z − x| < ρ}. Then the set {x : x ∈ F and μ(X(x) ∩ B_ρ(x)) ≤ s} is closed.
subproblem.lean_statement: ∀ (P : ℕ) (μ : Measure (Euclid P)) (F : Set (Euclid P)) (Q : Euclid P → Submodule ℝ (Euclid P)) (ρ : ℝ) (s : ℝ≥0∞), IsClosed F → ContinuousOn (fun x => (Q x).starProjection) F → IsClosed {x | x ∈ F ∧ μ ({z | 2 * ‖(Q x).starProjection (z - x)‖ < ‖z - x‖} ∩ ball x ρ) ≤ s}
subproblem.natural_proof:
Source: parent proof, step 4(ii). Closedness of the sets C_k there replaces the measurability of Simon's functions q_k (Simon Ch. 3, proof of 1.6 “⇐”, (7)–(8)). For w ∈ ℝ^P write L_w := p_{Q(w)} and S(w) := X(w) ∩ B_ρ(w).

1. Reduction. ℝ^P is a metric space, so it suffices to prove sequential closedness. Let x_i → x with x_i ∈ F and μ(S(x_i)) ≤ s for all i ∈ ℕ. Since F is closed, x ∈ F. It remains to show μ(S(x)) ≤ s.
2. Openness. For each w, the maps z ↦ 2|L_w(z − w)| and z ↦ |z − w| are continuous (L_w is a continuous linear map), so X(w) = {z : 2|L_w(z − w)| < |z − w|} is open. B_ρ(w) is open. Hence every S(w) is open, in particular Borel.
3. Convergence of the projections. The x_i lie in F and converge to x ∈ F, and w ↦ L_w is continuous on F, so ‖L_{x_i} − L_x‖ → 0 in the operator norm.
4. Pointwise liminf bound. Fix z ∈ S(x). We have L_{x_i}(z − x_i) − L_x(z − x) = (L_{x_i} − L_x)(z − x_i) + L_x(x − x_i). Hence |L_{x_i}(z − x_i) − L_x(z − x)| ≤ ‖L_{x_i} − L_x‖·|z − x_i| + ‖L_x‖·|x − x_i| → 0, because ‖L_{x_i} − L_x‖ → 0, |z − x_i| → |z − x| stays bounded, ‖L_x‖ ≤ 1 is fixed and |x − x_i| → 0. Also |z − x_i| → |z − x|. So 2|L_{x_i}(z − x_i)| − |z − x_i| → 2|L_x(z − x)| − |z − x| < 0 and |z − x_i| → |z − x| < ρ. For all sufficiently large i, therefore, 2|L_{x_i}(z − x_i)| < |z − x_i| and |z − x_i| < ρ, i.e. z ∈ S(x_i). So 1_{S(x_i)}(z) = 1 for all large i, and liminf_i 1_{S(x_i)}(z) = 1 = 1_{S(x)}(z). For z ∉ S(x), trivially 1_{S(x)}(z) = 0 ≤ liminf_i 1_{S(x_i)}(z). Thus 1_{S(x)} ≤ liminf_i 1_{S(x_i)} pointwise.
5. Fatou. The functions 1_{S(x_i)} are measurable (step 2) and nonnegative. Fatou's lemma (Mathlib `lintegral_liminf_le`) gives μ(S(x)) = ∫ 1_{S(x)} dμ ≤ ∫ liminf_i 1_{S(x_i)} dμ ≤ liminf_i ∫ 1_{S(x_i)} dμ = liminf_i μ(S(x_i)) ≤ s, the last step because every term is ≤ s. Hence x belongs to the set, which is therefore closed. ∎
proof_key_steps: Sequential closedness: x_i ∈ F, x_i → x, μ(S(x_i)) ≤ s; x ∈ F since F is closed.
Each S(w) = X(w) ∩ B_ρ(w) is open, hence Borel.
Continuity of w ↦ p_{Q(w)} on F gives operator-norm convergence, so every z ∈ S(x) lies in S(x_i) for all large i: 1_{S(x)} ≤ liminf 1_{S(x_i)}.

audit.reason: The exact type correctly expresses operator-norm continuity of orthogonal projections on closed F. The proof establishes open measurable cone slices, convergence under evaluation at moving vectors, persistence of both strict inequalities, and the Fatou bound. It works for arbitrary μ and all stated ρ and s, with no circular dependency.

subproblem.title: Egoroff-type uniformization of eventually-true closed conditions on a set of finite measure (parent steps 4(iii)–5)
subproblem.statement: Let P ∈ ℕ, μ a measure on ℝ^P (Borel σ-algebra), F ⊆ ℝ^P a Borel set with μ(F) < ∞, and (T_ρ)_{ρ∈ℝ} a family of subsets of ℝ^P. Suppose T_ρ is closed for every ρ > 0, and every x ∈ F lies in T_ρ for all sufficiently small ρ > 0, i.e. there is r > 0 with x ∈ T_ρ for all ρ ∈ (0, r) (Lean: ∀ᶠ ρ in 𝓝[>] 0, x ∈ T ρ). Then for every η ∈ (0, ∞] (η ≠ 0) there are E ⊆ F and δ > 0 such that μ(F ∖ E) < η and x ∈ T_ρ for all x ∈ E and all ρ ∈ (0, δ).
subproblem.lean_statement: ∀ (P : ℕ) (μ : Measure (Euclid P)) (F : Set (Euclid P)) (T : ℝ → Set (Euclid P)), MeasurableSet F → μ F ≠ ∞ → (∀ ρ : ℝ, 0 < ρ → IsClosed (T ρ)) → (∀ x ∈ F, ∀ᶠ ρ in 𝓝[>] (0 : ℝ), x ∈ T ρ) → ∀ η : ℝ≥0∞, η ≠ 0 → ∃ (E : Set (Euclid P)) (δ : ℝ), E ⊆ F ∧ 0 < δ ∧ μ (F \ E) < η ∧ ∀ x ∈ E, ∀ ρ : ℝ, 0 < ρ → ρ < δ → x ∈ T ρ
subproblem.natural_proof:
Source: parent proof, steps 4(iii) and 5 (the increasing closed sets G_k and the Egoroff step). This is Simon Ch. 3, proof of 1.6 “⇐”, (7)–(9), with Egoroff's theorem (8) carried out on sets. The parent applies it with F := the compact set produced by Lusin and T_ρ := A_ρ ∩ C_ρ, the set of points satisfying the lower-density and cone bounds at radius ρ.

1. The sets G_k. For k ∈ ℕ let δ_k := 1/(k + 1) > 0 and G_k := F ∩ ⋂_{ρ ∈ (0, δ_k)} T_ρ. Every ρ in the intersection is positive, so ⋂_{ρ ∈ (0, δ_k)} T_ρ is an intersection of closed sets, hence closed. Since F is Borel, G_k is Borel.
2. Monotonicity. δ_{k+1} < δ_k, so (0, δ_{k+1}) ⊆ (0, δ_k) and therefore G_k ⊆ G_{k+1}: a point of F lying in T_ρ for all ρ ∈ (0, δ_k) lies in T_ρ for all ρ ∈ (0, δ_{k+1}).
3. Exhaustion. ⋃_k G_k = F. Clearly G_k ⊆ F. Conversely let x ∈ F. The sets (0, r), r > 0, form a basis of the filter 𝓝[>] 0, so the hypothesis gives r > 0 with x ∈ T_ρ for all ρ ∈ (0, r). By the Archimedean property choose k with 1/(k + 1) < r. Every ρ ∈ (0, δ_k) satisfies ρ < r, so x ∈ T_ρ; hence x ∈ G_k.
4. Continuity from above. The Borel sets D_k := F ∖ G_k decrease in k (step 2), ⋂_k D_k = F ∖ ⋃_k G_k = ∅ (step 3), and μ(D_0) ≤ μ(F) < ∞. By continuity of measure from above (Mathlib `tendsto_measure_iInter_atTop`), μ(F ∖ G_k) → μ(∅) = 0 as k → ∞.
5. Choice of E and δ. Since η > 0, step 4 gives k with μ(F ∖ G_k) < η. Put E := G_k ⊆ F and δ := δ_k > 0. If x ∈ E and 0 < ρ < δ, then x ∈ ⋂_{ρ' ∈ (0, δ_k)} T_ρ', so x ∈ T_ρ. ∎
proof_key_steps: G_k := F ∩ ⋂_{0<ρ<1/(k+1)} T_ρ is Borel (F Borel, intersection of closed sets).
G_k increases with k and ⋃_k G_k = F, by the eventual membership hypothesis and the Archimedean property.
Continuity from above for F ∖ G_k ↓ ∅ with μ(F) < ∞: μ(F ∖ G_k) → 0.
Choose k with μ(F ∖ G_k) < η; E := G_k, δ := 1/(k+1).

audit.reason: Prose and type agree. Arbitrary intersections of closed Tρ make Gk Borel without joint measurability in ρ. Eventual membership gives exhaustion, while finite μ(F) permits continuity from above for F minus Gk. Choosing one index supplies the strict measure bound and common positive radius, including infinite tolerance. The proof is complete and independent.

subproblem.title: Lusin's theorem for an a.e. strongly measurable map, keeping an a.e. property (parent steps 1–2; the closed set F of Simon Ch. 3, proof of 1.6, (4))
subproblem.statement: Let P ∈ ℕ and let Y be a pseudo-metrizable, second-countable topological space. Let μ be a measure on ℝ^P (Borel σ-algebra), A ⊆ ℝ^P a Borel set with μ(A) < ∞, f : ℝ^P → Y a map that is almost everywhere strongly measurable with respect to μ⌞A, and p a property of points of ℝ^P that holds μ⌞A-almost everywhere. Then for every η ∈ (0, ∞] (η ≠ 0) there is a compact set K ⊆ A with μ(A ∖ K) < η such that p(x) holds for every x ∈ K and f is continuous on K.
subproblem.lean_statement: ∀ (P : ℕ) {Y : Type} [TopologicalSpace Y] [TopologicalSpace.PseudoMetrizableSpace Y] [SecondCountableTopology Y] (μ : Measure (Euclid P)) (A : Set (Euclid P)) (f : Euclid P → Y) (p : Euclid P → Prop), MeasurableSet A → μ A ≠ ∞ → AEStronglyMeasurable f (μ.restrict A) → (∀ᵐ x ∂(μ.restrict A), p x) → ∀ η : ℝ≥0∞, η ≠ 0 → ∃ K : Set (Euclid P), IsCompact K ∧ K ⊆ A ∧ μ (A \ K) < η ∧ (∀ x ∈ K, p x) ∧ ContinuousOn f K
subproblem.natural_proof:
Source: parent proof, steps 1–2 (a Borel set of good points; Lusin), which produce the closed set F of Simon Ch. 3, proof of 1.6 “⇐”, (4) (chapter-03.txt lines 168–172). The parent applies it with μ := Hⁿ, A := M, Y := L(ℝ^P) with the operator norm, f(x) := p_{Q(x)} and p(x) := “M has approximate tangent space Q(x) at x”.

1. A Borel representative. Since f is a.e. strongly measurable for μ⌞A, there is a strongly measurable g : ℝ^P → Y with f = g μ⌞A-almost everywhere (Mathlib `AEStronglyMeasurable.mk`, `stronglyMeasurable_mk`, `ae_eq_mk`). Give Y its Borel σ-algebra, so every open subset of Y is measurable. Y is pseudo-metrizable, so the strongly measurable map g (a pointwise limit of simple functions) is measurable (Mathlib `StronglyMeasurable.measurable`).
2. A Borel set of good points. Let Z := {x ∈ ℝ^P : f(x) ≠ g(x) or p(x) fails}. Both {f ≠ g} and {x : p(x) fails} are μ⌞A-null, so μ⌞A(Z) = 0. Since A is measurable, μ⌞A(Z) = μ(Z ∩ A) (Mathlib `Measure.restrict_apply'`), so μ(Z ∩ A) = 0. Choose a measurable N ⊇ Z ∩ A with μ(N) = 0 (Mathlib `exists_measurable_superset_of_null`) and put A₁ := A ∖ N. Then A₁ is measurable and μ(A₁) ≤ μ(A) < ∞. Every x ∈ A₁ satisfies f(x) = g(x) and p(x): x ∈ A and x ∉ N ⊇ Z ∩ A, so x ∉ Z.
3. Lusin. Apply the sibling lusin (Lusin's theorem, compact form) to the measure μ, the measurable set A₁ (μ(A₁) < ∞), the measurable map g : ℝ^P → Y (Y is second countable and its open sets are measurable) and the tolerance η ≠ 0. This gives a compact K ⊆ A₁ with μ(A₁ ∖ K) < η such that g is continuous on K.
4. Verification. K is compact and K ⊆ A₁ ⊆ A. Every x ∈ K lies in A₁, so p(x) holds and f(x) = g(x). Hence f and g agree on K, and f is continuous on K because g is (Mathlib `ContinuousOn.congr`). Finally A ∖ K ⊆ N ∪ (A₁ ∖ K): if x ∈ A ∖ K and x ∉ N, then x ∈ A₁ ∖ K. By subadditivity, μ(A ∖ K) ≤ μ(N) + μ(A₁ ∖ K) = 0 + μ(A₁ ∖ K) < η. ∎
proof_key_steps: Replace f by a strongly measurable, hence Borel measurable, representative g with f = g μ⌞A-a.e. (Y with its Borel σ-algebra).
The bad set Z = {f ≠ g} ∪ {¬p} has μ(Z ∩ A) = 0. A measurable null hull N gives A₁ := A ∖ N of full measure, on which f = g and p holds.
Lusin (sibling lusin) for g on A₁ with tolerance η: compact K ⊆ A₁ with μ(A₁ ∖ K) < η and g continuous on K.
f = g on K, so f is continuous on K; p holds on K; μ(A ∖ K) ≤ μ(N) + μ(A₁ ∖ K) < η.

audit.reason: All hypotheses match the type. Pseudo-metrizability justifies measurability of the strongly measurable representative after choosing the Borel σ-algebra. Restriction equality and a measurable null hull preserve the arbitrary a.e. property pointwise. Applying lusin and transferring continuity proves every conclusion. The sole child dependency, lusin, is correctly directed.
